name: Amasa
bio:
Amasa was the son of Abigail, David's sister, and so a cousin to Joab and Abishai; when Absalom launched his rebellion, he appointed Amasa commander of his army in Joab's place (2 Samuel 17:25). After Absalom's defeat, David offered Amasa Joab's position permanently, declaring, "You are my own flesh and blood. God deal with me, be it ever so severely, if you are not the commander of my army for life in place of Joab" (2 Samuel 19:13).

When Sheba's revolt broke out, David ordered Amasa to muster Judah's forces within three days, but Amasa took longer than the time set for him, so David sent Abishai and Joab's men in pursuit of Sheba instead (2 Samuel 20:4-7). At the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa met them on the road; Joab, his sword concealed and falling loose from its sheath as he approached, took Amasa by the beard with his right hand as if to kiss him — and with his left thrust the sword into Amasa's belly, spilling his insides to the ground. Amasa died without a second blow, lying in his own blood in the middle of the highway until one of Joab's men dragged his body into a field and covered it, so that the army would stop gawking and continue the pursuit of Sheba (2 Samuel 20:8-13) — a second kinsman, after Abner, murdered by Joab under the guise of a friendly greeting.
